Sogon is a macOS dictation and meeting-recording app that lives in the menu bar. It turns your speech into text, optionally polishes it with an LLM, and puts it where your cursor was before you started speaking.

Task Press Result Put speech at the cursor Hold ⌃⇧R, speak, release Transcribed, corrected text lands at your original cursor Polish text you typed ⌃⇧T Text in the input window is corrected and inserted Translate a selection ⌘C twice The original and the translation appear in a window Act on a selection ⌃⇧C A grid of correct, structure, translate, convert, Notes, and search actions Insert a saved phrase ⌃⇧V Pick a snippet and insert it at the cursor Ask while showing your screen ⌃⇧S The captured image and your words are pasted into the target app Record a meeting Menu bar icon → Session recording Record, then transcribe and create minutes or a verbatim transcript Translating with ⌘C twice and the ⌃⇧S screen region are off by default. Each guide explains how to turn them on.

An Apple Silicon (arm64) Mac on macOS 14 or later Microphone and Accessibility permissions For correction and translation, one LLM provider (Amazon Bedrock, OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Groq, or local MLX) Speech recognition runs on your Mac by default. Without an LLM, Sogon inserts the transcription as is.

Install First launch and permissions Your first dictation Connect an LLM Getting from install to your first dictation takes about 10 minutes. The longest step is downloading the speech model (about 1.6GB).
documents.s: New here? Read in this order

documents.t: With default settings, audio and transcriptions stay on your Mac. If you choose a cloud LLM or turn on AWS Transcribe, Sogon sends text or audio to that service. You'll find the full list of conditions in Data and privacy.

With an LLM connected, Sogon fixes misrecognitions and spacing in your dictation, and ⌘C twice translation plus the correct, structure, and translate actions in the ⌃⇧C grid start working. Without one, Sogon inserts the transcription as is.

Pick one in Settings → LLM → Correction Provider → Provider. Provider Authentication Where to get it Good when Amazon Bedrock Bedrock API key and region Bedrock API keys in the AWS console Your company only allows Bedrock. One key covers Nova and Claude. Anthropic Claude A key starting with sk-ant- Anthropic Console You want the fastest Claude Google Gemini Gemini API key Google AI Studio You want to start on the free tier OpenAI (GPT) Codex CLI sign-in Run codex login in a terminal You already use the Codex CLI Groq Cloud Groq API key Groq Console You need fast responses Local MLX None The model is downloaded to your Mac You do not want text to leave your Mac The default is None (use raw transcript).

Open Settings → LLM. Choose the service in Provider. Enter the key in the authentication section that appears. For Bedrock, also enter the Region (for example us-east-1). Choose a model in the model section. The default is fine to start. Check that the correction provider's Status turns ready. Keys are stored in this Mac's Keychain.

Choose how Sogon polishes text in the Correction Mode section of the same tab. Mode What it does Standard (STT Correction) Fixes misrecognitions, spacing, and English term spelling. Keeps your tone. Filler Removal Removes fillers such as "um" and "uh". Structured Organizes what you said into lists and paragraphs. Custom Uses a prompt template you choose. If a correction changes more than half of the original, Sogon discards it and inserts the original (Standard and Filler Removal modes). For text longer than 1,500 characters, Sogon inserts it without correction.

Do your first dictation again. Expand the new item in Settings → History → Dictation. If Compare appears, correction was applied. You can switch between the corrected text and the original. If the correction changed nothing, Compare does not appear. That's not a failure.

Symptom What to check Status shows an error Paste the key again. For Bedrock, check that the model is available in that region. The translation window says No LLM provider is set up The provider is None. Connect one with the steps above. You chose OpenAI and see Signed out Run codex login in a terminal and reopen Sogon. Correction never happens In the quick controls, check that Enable correction is on in the engine section. With it off, the raw text is inserted even when a provider is chosen. Models and speed comparisons per provider are in LLM providers.
Dictate one sentence into Notes or a text editor. The default recording mode is Push to Talk: Sogon records while you hold the shortcut and transcribes when you release it.

Open a text editor and click where the text should go. Press and hold ⌃⇧R (Control + Shift + R). Watch the Voice Bar appear at the bottom center of the screen and check that the input level moves. Say "The meeting starts at three today." Release the keys. The Voice Bar shows the transcribing state and disappears, and the text appears at the cursor. The first recording takes a few extra seconds while the speech model loads into memory. Later recordings are faster.

If the sentence is in your editor, it worked. Inserted text lives in Settings → History → Dictation. Click the menu bar icon to see it under Last Transcription in the quick controls. Without an LLM, the transcription goes in as is. To fix spelling and terms, connect an LLM.

If you prefer to press once to start and again to stop, change Settings → General → Recording → Recording Mode to Toggle. Change the shortcut itself in Global Shortcut in the same section. To use only the mouse, right-click the menu bar icon. Right-click always starts on the first click and stops on the second, whatever the recording mode.

To keep the result out of your document during recording or transcription, press ⌃⇧⌫ (Control + Shift + Delete) or the cancel button on the Voice Bar. esc is passed through to other apps, so it doesn't cancel.

Symptom What to check Pressing the shortcut does not show the Voice Bar In Settings → General → Permissions, check that Accessibility shows Granted. If you just granted it, relaunch Sogon. Nothing happens only in a terminal such as iTerm2 Secure Keyboard Entry in that app blocks global shortcuts. Turn it off there. The Voice Bar appears but the input level doesn't move In Settings → General → Input, check that Capture my microphone is on and the macOS input device is right. Text is only on the clipboard, not at the cursor You may not have finished the tutorial with Get started. Open Settings → General → Tutorial → Show again, go to the last screen, and press Get started. Text goes into a different app With several displays, clicking the menu bar on another display makes that display's app the target. Use the shortcut, or click the menu bar on the display where the text should go. More symptoms are covered in Troubleshooting. Next: Connect an LLM

The tutorial window opens on first launch. Go through the eight steps and press Get started on the last screen. Press Get started at the end If you close the tutorial window with its close button, setup counts as unfinished. In that state dictated text is only copied to the clipboard instead of being inserted at the cursor, and the tutorial opens again on the next launch. Skipping individual steps with Skip is fine.

Step Screen title What to do 1 A menu bar app that turns speech into text Read the introduction and press Next. 2 Grant permissions Allow Microphone and Accessibility. 3 Download the speech model Pick a model. Large v3 Turbo is the recommended default. 4 Groq API key (optional) Only for cloud speech recognition. Usually leave it blank. 5 LLM correction (good to know) An overview of correction engines and modes. You set this up later. 6 Where should the app appear Choose the menu bar, the Dock, or both. 7 What else you can do One screen with the features beyond dictation and their shortcuts. Nothing to set up. 8 You are set Check the recording shortcut and readiness, then press Get started.

Two permissions are required. The rest are only needed for specific features. Permission Why Without it Microphone Recording your voice Recording does not start. Accessibility Global shortcuts and pasting at the cursor Shortcuts do nothing and text is not inserted. System Audio (Screen Recording) Recording sound played on your Mac, such as the other side of a call Only the microphone is recorded. Automation · Google Chrome / iTerm2 Returning to the original tab, field, or terminal session after recording Sogon only activates the app and pastes. On the permissions screen, press Grant next to Microphone and allow it in the macOS dialog. Press Grant next to Accessibility. When System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility opens, turn Sogon on. Return to the tutorial and check that both items show Granted. Sogon only asks for permissions when you press a button. Launching the app or starting a recording never opens a permission dialog. To check later, open Settings → General → Permissions.

Picking a model in step 3 starts the download right away. You can press Next while it downloads, and closing the window doesn't stop it. Model Size Choose it when Large v3 Turbo compressed about 632MB You want the quickest start and to save disk space Large v3 Turbo about 1.6GB You are not sure (app default) Large v3 about 3.1GB Accuracy matters more than speed If you skip without picking a model, the default model is downloaded on your first recording. You can change models later in Settings → STT.

The Readiness list on the last screen shows the microphone, the global shortcut, and the speech model. When all are green, Everything is ready appears. If you see Permission is granted but the shortcut listener is not attached yet, press Get started, then quit and relaunch Sogon.
Open it any time from Settings → General → Tutorial → Show again. It doesn't reset your current settings. Next: Your first dictation
Download the DMG and move it into /Applications. No sign-in and no extra tooling are needed.
Make sure your Mac has Apple Silicon. Sogon doesn't run on Intel Macs. Make sure you are on macOS 14 or later.

Open the latest release in a browser. Download Sogon.dmg (Apple Silicon, notarized) from the latest release. If Sogon is running, click the menu bar icon and press Quit (⌘Q) at the bottom of the quick controls. Open the DMG and drag Sogon.app into the Applications folder. Launch /Applications/Sogon.app. Releases are signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple. You don't need to clear the quarantine attribute with xattr or lower your security settings.

On first launch macOS asks for permissions. Sogon needs two: Microphone — for recording and dictation. Accessibility — to type text at the cursor. Enable Sogon under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility.
The Sogon icon appears in the menu bar. With default settings it also appears in the Dock. On first launch the tutorial window opens. Continue with First launch and permissions.

Symptom What to do "Sogon.app" cannot be opened warning The build is notarized. Control-click the app in Finder and choose Open, or press Open Anyway in System Settings → Privacy & Security. Dictation does not type at the cursor Check that Sogon is enabled under System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility. The menu bar icon is not visible It may be hidden behind the notch or other menu bar apps. Click the Dock icon to open Settings. Updates install the same way. When a new version exists, a one-line notice appears in the quick controls and in Settings → Status. Sogon doesn't download updates automatically.
Any tool that can open a sogon:// URL can start and stop dictation. Opening the URL does not change the frontmost app, so the result goes into the app where your cursor is now.

open "sogon://toggle" # start / stop open "sogon://push" # start (ignored if already recording) open "sogon://release" # stop (ignored if not recording) Put push and release on two buttons to get Push to Talk. These three commands always work, regardless of settings. Tool How to set it up Raycast Create a Quicklink with the URL and assign a hotkey. Stream Deck Put the URL in System: Open. Keyboard Maestro, Shortcuts Use an open-URL action. There is no URL to start or end a meeting session, so an external tool can't cut a long recording by accident.

open "sogon://text?text=we need validation here" Sogon corrects the text and puts it on the clipboard. It's never inserted at the cursor. When done, the Voice Bar shows Copied to clipboard for a few seconds; paste with ⌘V. This works only after you turn on Allow text correction from external tools in Settings → General → External Tools. It's off by default, and Sogon ignores requests while it's off. When on, text from other programs also goes through correction and may be sent to a cloud LLM, overwrites your clipboard, and is added to the dictation history. Things to watch for: Put Korean in as is, or percent-encode everything. Mixing the two leaves %20 as literal text. Don't use + for spaces. + arrives as a character. Text longer than 1,500 characters is rejected. The caller can't tell when correction finishes. This isn't suited to programs that need the result back.

AWS Transcribe uploads the session audio to S3, transcribes it, and returns each word with a time and a speaker. The result is stored in the same place as Attach speakers, so the Speakers tab, naming, and exports work as they do there. You don't enter an attendee count, and up to 30 speakers are separated. Audio leaves your machine The entire meeting audio is uploaded to S3, and Transcribe and S3 charges apply. Sogon deletes the uploaded audio when the job ends, whether it succeeds or fails. The feature is off by default.

Install the aws CLI: brew install awscli Sign in with the AWS profile you will use: aws sso login --profile <name> In Settings → STT → AWS Transcribe, turn on Allow transcription with AWS Transcribe. Choose the AWS profile and enter the S3 bucket and Region. The region must match the bucket. Check that the status under the profile shows Signed in. Status Meaning Signed in — expires in 3 hours Ready to use. The token expired but can be refreshed Just use it; the CLI refreshes the token. No new sign-in is needed. Sign-in required Run the aws sso login command shown on screen in a terminal. The AWS CLI is not installed Do step 1.

Expand the session in Settings → History → Meetings. In Transcript, press Transcribe with AWS. If the bucket you entered does not exist, Sogon says so and offers Create <bucket>. Check the name and press it; the bucket is created with public access blocked, default encryption, and a rule that deletes objects under sogon/ after 7 days. When it finishes, view the result in the Speakers tab. Uploading a session that was already transcribed asks for confirmation first. The result is replaced and you are charged again. Names you gave speakers are kept.

A recording in several segments is merged and uploaded as one file, because separate uploads would number speakers differently in each part. In sessions that recorded both the microphone and system audio, Sogon uploads only the system audio track. When the transcription language is Auto-detect, Sogon sends the job as Korean. If another account already uses the bucket name, Sogon asks you to choose another name.
Dictation runs in four stages: record, transcribe, correct, insert. The finished text goes into the app and field your cursor was in when recording started.

Entry point Behavior ⌃⇧R Push to Talk by default. Records while held and transcribes on release. ⌃⇧D Press once to start and again to stop, whatever the recording mode. Right-click the menu bar icon Press once to start and again to stop. Start Recording in the quick controls In the window that opens when you left-click the menu bar icon. sogon://toggle Start and stop from another tool. See External tools. Choose Push to Talk or Toggle in Settings → General → Recording → Recording Mode. Set the right-click action in Settings → General → General → Right-click the menu bar icon: Start/stop dictation (default), Start/stop meeting recording, or Do nothing.

Sogon remembers the app and field at the moment recording starts and pastes there. Pasting uses the clipboard and ⌘V. Your previous clipboard contents are restored shortly after. If there's nowhere to paste or pasting fails, the result stays on the clipboard and the Voice Bar says so. Paste it yourself with ⌘V. To return all the way to a Chrome tab and field or an iTerm2 session (including tmux windows and panes), turn on both switches in Settings → General → Context Restore and grant the Automation permission. With several displays Clicking the menu bar on another display makes macOS bring that display's app forward, and that app becomes the target. To insert into the original app, use the shortcut or click the menu bar on that app's display.

You can start a new recording while the previous one is still being corrected. Sogon processes several utterances at once but inserts them in the order you spoke them. Insertion pauses while you record and resumes when you stop.

Method Notes ⌃⇧⌫ The default cancel shortcut. Change it in Settings → General → Recording → Cancel Shortcut. Cancel button on the Voice Bar Visible only while recording or processing. Quick controls and Settings → Status Appear only when there is something to cancel. Canceling discards the captured audio and the result, and inserts nothing. Stop Recording does the opposite: it transcribes and inserts what was recorded so far. esc does not cancel. ⌃⇧⌫ does nothing when only a meeting session is running, so a single keystroke cannot throw away a long recording. To cancel a meeting session, press cancel in the quick controls or Settings → Status and confirm.

⌃⇧D is a press-to-start, press-to-stop dictation regardless of the recording mode. It also works while a meeting session is running; in that case the text goes only to the cursor and isn't added to the session. The order matters: start the session first, then add dictation. You can't start a session while dictating. During a session, Stop Recording in the quick controls stops the session, so press ⌃⇧D again to stop only the dictation.

Choose these in Settings → General → Input. Setting Default Notes Capture my microphone On Records your voice. Capture system audio Off Records sound played on your Mac. Needs the Screen Recording permission. Remove playback from mic On Reduces speaker sound leaking back into the mic and being transcribed twice. Audio Input Channel Auto (downmix) Picks the channel on multichannel audio devices. Transcription Language Korean Auto-detect, Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, or Portuguese. When both sources are recorded, the result is labeled [마이크] (microphone) and [시스템 오디오] (system audio).

Turn on Line break on pauses in Settings → General → Dictation Formatting to start a new line where you pause. The pause threshold is 0.6 seconds and adjustable. It works only with the WhisperKit engine.

The bar at the bottom center of the active display while recording and processing. It does not take keyboard focus, so you can keep typing in the target app. Turn off Settings → General → General → Show recording overlay to hide it. Choose Overlay opacity from Opaque, Medium, and Translucent. The eye icon in the quick controls hides it for the current run only. Click the menu bar icon to bring it back.

Settings → History holds three lists. Use the switcher at the top to view Dictation, Meetings, or Translations. Only lists with content appear in the switcher. List What is kept Retention Dictation The latest 100: corrected text, original, recording (when kept), screen capture Follows the Retention setting Meetings Session logs, outputs, segment audio Follows the Retention setting Translations Original, translation, model, tokens Fixed at 7 days, latest 100

Type a word or a date in the search field above the list, and all three lists are filtered together. With several words, only items containing all of them remain, for example meeting lambda. Dates can be written as 2026-08-27, 08-27, or 8월 27일. Dictation and meetings are searched by preview and date only. The full text of long dictations and full meeting transcriptions are not searched. Translations are searched in full, original and translation. Korean initial-consonant search isn't supported.

Copy the text. If the recording was kept, listen with Play. Turn on keeping recordings with Keep audio recording in the quick controls. It is off by default. Items corrected by the LLM offer Compare to highlight changed words and switch to the original. Items from a screen region offer View screen and Copy screen. Send to Notes creates a new Apple Notes note, including the screen capture when there is one.
documents.s: What you can do with a dictation item

documents.t: In Retention at the bottom of the History tab, turn on Auto-delete old history and choose a period. The default is to never delete automatically. Sogon removes expired items when the app starts and when new history is added. Translations always use 7 days, regardless of this setting. In the same place, if leftover recording folders that were never used for transcription are found, their count and size appear, and Reclaim audio deletes them. Sogon never does this while recording.

Deleting a single item asks for confirmation, and the message tells you which files go with it. Deleting a meeting item removes its session log, outputs, and remaining audio. Without the audio, the session cannot be transcribed again. Each list has a clear-all button: Clear all dictation history, Clear all meeting history, Clear all translation history.

Transcribe files from a recorder app or a video-call tool with Sogon. The result is the same kind of history item as a meeting you recorded, so minutes, verbatim documents, speakers, and exports all work.

Open Settings → History. Press Import files. With no meeting history, a separate Import files section is shown. With meeting history, choose Meetings in the switcher at the top; the button is at the head of the list. Choose files. You can choose up to 20 at a time. A progress row appears for each file. When done, a new item appears in the meeting list with the file name shown. Expand the item and press Create minutes document or Create verbatim document.

mp3, wav, m4a, aac, aiff, caf, flac, mp4, mov For video, only the first audio track is used. Original files are only read; they are never moved or deleted. If some files are unsupported or unreadable, only those are skipped and the rest are imported. Skipped files are listed. Choosing 21 or more imports nothing.

Sogon transcribes files one at a time; the rest wait. You can start dictation or a meeting recording while importing. When live work is waiting, the import pauses for a moment and then resumes. Canceling a waiting file removes it right away. Canceling during transcription keeps what was transcribed so far as a history item. Clear finished progress rows with Clear finished.

Meeting recording is a separate path from dictation. The transcription is not inserted at the cursor; it accumulates in Settings → History → Meetings. By default you record first and start transcription after the meeting.

To keep the other side of a call, turn on system audio. In the quick controls, turn on System Audio under Audio Sources, and press Request System Audio Permission the first time. Headphones keep other people's voices from leaking back into your mic, which gives a cleaner result. With speakers, the same speech can be captured once on each track. Check your free disk space. One track takes about 1.9MB per minute, twice that with both sources. If free space drops below 500MB, the session ends automatically.

Click the menu bar icon to open the quick controls. In the Session recording block, check that Record only, do not transcribe is on. It's on by default. Press Start Recording (transcribe later). When the meeting ends, press Stop Recording. A session can record up to 3 hours. If the app quits unexpectedly while recording, the audio up to that point is kept and the session reappears in the history on the next launch.

Open Settings → History and choose Meetings in the switcher at the top. The new session is marked Awaiting transcription. Expand it. Check the number and size of the kept audio segments and press Start transcription. Progress shows as Transcribing 3 / 12 and continues even if you close Settings. You don't choose an output type at this point. When it finishes, choose what to view in the selector at the top of the item: Transcript, Speakers, Minutes output, or Verbatim output. Speakers appears only when speakers can be attached. Press Create minutes document or Create verbatim document. Take the result with Export .txt, Export .md, or Send to Notes. Output Contents Needs an LLM Transcript The transcription in time order No Verbatim The transcript split into paragraphs at pauses. With Clean up transcript (LLM) on, sentences and punctuation are tidied too. Optional Minutes A document with four sections: summary, decisions, action items, and other Yes One session can have both minutes and a verbatim document. You don't need to transcribe again. If the transcription is shorter than 200 characters, Sogon suggests a verbatim transcript instead of minutes. You can continue with Make minutes anyway.

To see the transcription during the meeting, turn off Record only, do not transcribe before starting, choose a Session type, and press Start Minutes Session or Start Verbatim Session. The session type cannot change while recording. Transcription is finalized in chunks of about 2–3 minutes. The first result appears after at least 2 minutes. It's not live captioning. In a verbatim session, Show session transcript shows the finalized text, and you can open it in a window that floats over your meeting. That window never takes keyboard focus. Turn on Settings → STT → Live preview to see unconfirmed text in gray within 2–5 seconds. It works only with WhisperKit and uses more CPU. It's off by default.

Audio from record-only sessions is kept after transcription, so you can Transcribe again with a better model later. To free space, use Delete audio on the item. Once deleted, the session cannot be transcribed again. You can expand an item and play its audio even before transcribing.
Attach who said what: Attach speakers Transcribe recordings you already have: Import files Dictate during a meeting: Dictation

Use this when you ask an agent or chat something like "what is this error" while pointing at your screen. Sogon never reads the captured image as text; it pastes the image as is, so nothing is sent to the cloud. Only the words you speak go through the LLM for correction.
Turn on Capture a screen region and talk about it (⌃⇧S) in Settings → General → External Tools. It's off by default, and while it's off ⌃⇧S does nothing.

Click the app where the question should go (an agent input, a chat box) to place the cursor. Press ⌃⇧S. A crosshair like ⌘⇧4 appears. Drag to select the region to show. A window showing the image opens and recording starts right away. Say your question. You can also type in the window's field. Press ⌃⇧S again or ⌘Return. The image is pasted into the original app first, then the corrected text. Press esc while selecting to cancel quietly. A tight region works best.

There are two pastes: a single ⌘V gives the receiving app only the image or only the text. If there's nowhere to paste, both stay on the clipboard and the Voice Bar says so. Click the image in the window to see it larger. The larger window has Copy and Save. Sogon keeps the capture with the dictation history. Expand the item in Settings → History → Dictation and use View screen or Copy screen. Change the shortcut in Settings → General → Recording → Screen Region Shortcut.
Select text and press ⌃⇧C to open a grid of actions. Pick one with a single key. Actions that rewrite the text show the result first and ask before replacing.

Select the text. Press ⌃⇧C. Check that the top of the grid shows the first line of the captured text and its character, word, and line counts. Press the key for the cell you want. Arrow keys and ⏎ work too. If nothing is selected, the grid doesn't open. Sogon briefly uses the clipboard to capture the selection and restores it right away.

Row Key Action First 1 Correct (Standard mode) 2 Structure 3 Translate (Korean↔English) 4 Aa conversions (13 kinds: case, spacing, camelCase, and more) Second q Google search (the first URL action) w Save as snippet e Copy to clipboard r Large type Third a Send to Notes s Ask a CLI (kiro-cli, claude, codex) after that URL actions you added and prompt templates enabled as actions The same key positions work while a Korean input source is active (2-Set Korean layout). Cells that can replace your selection carry a small orange dot.

1 Correct, 2 Structure, 3 Translate, and template cells go through the LLM. When the result arrives, a comparison window opens. Key Action ⏎ or Replace Replace the selection with the result. This cannot be undone. c or Copy Put the result on the clipboard only. esc Discard. The original stays as it was. Pressing esc while waiting discards the request, and a late response never overwrites your text. The translate cell also shows the model and tokens in the result window. Without an LLM provider, 1 becomes Set up an LLM and 2 and 3 are empty. Aa conversions work without an LLM.

r shows the selection full screen in a monospaced font. It helps you tell l, 1, I and 0, O apart when copying a code or account number to another device. Resize with +/− and reset with 0. Any key or click closes it.

a Send to Notes: creates a new note in the default Apple Notes folder. The first use asks for the Automation permission. s Ask a CLI: in the sub-grid, choose 1 kiro-cli, 2 claude, or 3 codex. A new iTerm2 window opens and the tool starts by reading your selection. iTerm2 and that CLI must be installed. URL actions: add them with New action under Settings → Snippets → Send-out actions. The selection replaces {query} in the address, for example obsidian://new?vault=MyVault&content={query}.

Turn on Use as a selection action while editing a prompt template in Settings → LLM, and the template appears after the third row. They're all off by default. The built-in templates were written for dictation, so running Meeting notes on a single paragraph turns that paragraph into meeting notes. Change the shortcut in Settings → General → Recording → Selection Action Shortcut.
Snippets save you from retyping the same account number, address, introduction, or template. They skip correction and go in exactly as saved.

There are two ways: Select the text, press ⌃⇧C, then press w (Save as snippet) in the grid. Enter a name and save. In Settings → Snippets, press Add and write a name and body. Turn on Suggest a name in Settings → Snippets to let the LLM propose names. It is off by default. When on, the first 500 characters of the text are sent to your LLM provider.

Put the cursor where the text should go. Press ⌃⇧V. Type part of the name or body to filter. Choose with ↑/↓ and press ⏎. Key Action ⏎ Insert the selected snippet at the cursor. ⌘1–⌘9 Insert the 1st to 9th visible item directly. Numbers follow the filtered list. ⌘⏎ Put it on the clipboard instead of the cursor. Use it where pasting cannot reach, such as remote desktops. esc Close without inserting. Snippets skip the dictation queue, so they go in immediately even during a meeting recording. Sogon doesn't add them to the dictation history.

In the Settings → Snippets list, select several with ⇧-click or ⌘-click and press ⌫ to delete them together. The confirmation shows how many will be deleted. The list keeps the order you set. Sogon never reorders it by usage. Several snippets can share a name. Change the shortcut in Settings → General → Recording → Snippet Shortcut. Sogon is not a clipboard history app. It never collects what you copy; it only keeps the phrases you save.

Attach times and speakers, such as [00:34] Speaker 2, to a transcribed meeting session. Sogon doesn't transcribe the text again, so this also works on past sessions. There are two ways: Method Requirements Does audio leave your Mac On-device speaker attribution macOS 26 or later, session audio No AWS Transcribe The aws CLI, an AWS account, turned on in Settings Yes, uploaded to S3

Expand the session in Settings → History → Meetings. If five or more people attended, enter the number in Attendees. Leave it blank for four or fewer. Press Attach speakers. The first time, an approximately 234MB diarization model is downloaded. Choose Speakers in the selector to see the result. If a result already exists when you enter a count, press Redo to apply it. Meetings with five or more people With the count blank, the app separates at most four speakers. If five or more attended and the count is blank, the speech of the missing people gets distributed among the others. When the result has exactly four speakers the screen says so; enter the count and press Redo.

Enter a name for each speaker in the Speakers tab, and the transcript and .txt/.md exports use it. Clear it to go back to the number. Names apply only to that session; Speaker 1 in the next meeting may be someone else.

In sessions that recorded both the microphone and system audio, Sogon treats the microphone side as one person, you, and splits only the system audio side into speakers. Even the same speaker gets a new timestamped line after a pause of more than 2 seconds. A time-match rate is shown next to the result. The lower it is, the more the times rely on estimation. Sogon removes speakers who spoke less than 2% of the total. Speakers don't appear in the minutes or verbatim outputs, because summarizing easily mixes up who said what. Export from the Speakers tab when you need speakers.
Use this for text you typed or pasted where speaking is not practical. Only speech recognition is skipped; correction, term preservation, and insertion work exactly as in dictation.

Click the field where the text should go. Press ⌃⇧T. The input window opens. Type or paste your text. Press ⌘Return. The corrected text lands where your cursor was before the window opened. esc closes the window without inserting anything. Open text input in the quick controls opens it too.

Press the window's Dictate button, or dictate with ⌃⇧R while the window is open, and Sogon appends the transcription to the field. Speak, fix it by hand, then submit with ⌘Return. Text you dictate this way only goes into the field and never touches your clipboard.

The window shows the provider and correction mode that will apply. Change correction settings in Settings → LLM, not in the window. If correction is off, the window says No correction — inserted as-is and inserts the original. The limit is 1,500 characters. The window shows the count and blocks you from submitting beyond it. Change the shortcut in Settings → General → Recording → Text Input Shortcut.

Select text and press ⌘C twice quickly. Sogon translates it and shows the result in a window. Korean goes to English and English to Korean. The default engine is Apple Translation, which runs on this Mac, so nothing leaves the Mac and no LLM is needed.

Turn on Translate the selection by pressing ⌘C twice in Settings → General → External Tools. It is off by default. Check Translation engine in the same place. Apple Translation (this Mac) (default): download the Korean·English language pack once. You can get it ahead of time with Download on the Korean·English language pack row right below; otherwise a download window appears on your first translation, and the selection is translated as soon as it finishes. After that it works offline. It needs macOS 26 or later; older systems translate with the LLM. macOS manages the pack, so System Settings → General → Language & Region → Translation Languages works too. If you already downloaded it for the Translate app or Safari, there is nothing to download. LLM provider: finish Connect an LLM. It uses the same provider and key as correction and reads mixed-language text in context better. Before you turn it on When on, Sogon watches every ⌘C. With Apple Translation nothing leaves this Mac. If you switch the engine to an LLM provider, the second ⌘C sends the copied text to that provider, so press ⌘C only once when copying passwords or private notes.

Select the text. Press ⌘C twice quickly. The interval follows the macOS double-click speed setting. Check the original and the translation in the window. Choose one of the following. Key Action c or Copy Put the translation on the clipboard. Your selection stays as it was. ⏎ or Replace Replace the text you selected with the translation. This cannot be undone. esc Close the window. The original stays as it was. ⌘C isn't intercepted, so after the two presses your clipboard still holds the original. The window also shows character and word counts and the engine used. With an LLM it also shows the actual model name and input→output tokens. Apple Translation doesn't count tokens.

Use it for text in images, PDF figures, or anything on screen you cannot select. Sogon reads the text in the region on this Mac (OCR) and translates it with the Translation engine above. Turn on Translate a screen region with ⌃⇧E in Settings → General → External Tools. It is off by default. Press ⌃⇧E and a crosshair appears. Drag over the text you want translated. esc cancels. The translation window shows the text that was read and its translation. Copy puts the translation on the clipboard. There is no Replace, since nothing was selected. Grabbing a whole app window full of buttons and menus scatters short labels and makes the translation awkward. Pick a tight region around the paragraph. Lines of one paragraph broken by line wraps are joined before translating. Over 1,500 characters, Sogon does not translate and asks for a smaller region. Successful translations go to the same translation history as ⌘C twice. The first use may ask for Screen Recording permission. Region selection uses the macOS screenshot tool.

Successful translations are kept in Settings → History → Translations. The original, the translation, the time, the model, and the tokens are saved. Sogon deletes records automatically after 7 days. Within those 7 days, it keeps only the latest 100. Turning translation off stops new records. Delete one at a time or all at once with Clear all translation history. Both ask for confirmation.

Symptom What to check Nothing appears after pressing twice Check that the translation switch in External Tools is on and that text is actually selected. With no selection there's nothing to copy, so nothing is translated. The download window could not finish Press Try again in that window, or download from Download in Settings → General → External Tools, or from System Settings → General → Language & Region → Translation Languages. No LLM provider is set up Appears when the engine is LLM provider. Choose a provider in Settings → LLM, or switch the engine to Apple Translation. Long text is not translated The limit is 1,500 characters. Select shorter parts. You can do the same translation, with the same engine, without turning on ⌘C twice by pressing 3 in the ⌃⇧C grid. With Apple Translation, 3 appears even without an LLM. See Act on a selection.

The Dictionary holds two tools for fixing terms that speech recognition often gets wrong. Manage them in Settings → Dictionary. Tool What it does Needs an LLM Corrections (from → to) Replaces from with to right after transcription and again after LLM correction. No Words Passes the active set's words to LLM correction as a glossary so their spelling is kept. Yes Corrections work even with the LLM turned off. For example, registering 람다 → Lambda replaces 람다 whenever it appears in a transcription.

Choose a set under Word Sets, or create one by entering a New set name. Enter glossary spellings in New word. To fix a misrecognized expression, fill in From and To under Corrections (from → to). Each set can be turned on and off. Turn off sets for topics you don't use.

The repository's docs/dictionaries/ has 18 Cloud/IT topic sets with 142 corrections. Use Choose… next to Sync file path to pick a JSON file. Press Import. Importing replaces Importing replaces your existing sets instead of merging. If you made your own sets, back them up with Export first.

Sogon doesn't pass registered terms to speech recognition as a prompt. Repetitive prompts turned out to make Korean transcriptions come back empty, so Sogon applies terms only through corrections and the LLM glossary.
How to connect is in Connect an LLM. This page collects the differences that help you choose.

Provider Models Notes Amazon Bedrock Nova Micro, Lite, Pro, Premier; Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5, Opus 5 One key for Nova and Claude. Round trips for short input were Haiku 1.9s, Sonnet 2.7s, Opus 3.3s (us-east-1). Anthropic Claude Four Claude models Faster than the same models through Bedrock: Haiku 1.3s, Sonnet 1.7s, Opus 2.7s. Google Gemini Default 3.5 Flash-Lite The most stable on the free tier. Often leaves out periods. OpenAI (GPT) GPT models Uses the Codex CLI sign-in (codex login). Groq Cloud Groq models Uses the same key as Groq STT. Local MLX A downloaded model Text never leaves your Mac. These timings were measured in one development environment and vary with network and region.

Mode What it does Original protection Standard (STT Correction) Fixes misrecognitions, spacing, and English term spelling If more than 50% of words change, the original is used. Filler Removal Removes fillers Same as above. Structured Organizes into lists and paragraphs Not applied, since changing the shape is expected. Custom Uses the prompt template you choose Not applied. After correction, English terms that were in the original but disappeared are restored, and the Dictionary corrections are applied once more.

Edit templates in Settings → LLM. There are three built-in templates: Template Use General correction Polishes dictation. LLM prompt Turns a request you described out loud into a structure that works well when pasted into an LLM. Meeting notes Used for the final pass of the minutes output. Set a default template for dictation and one for minutes. Preview results with sample input. Deleting a template asks for confirmation. Deleted built-in templates come back with Restore built-ins; user templates cannot be recovered. Updating the app does not change built-in template text you already have. To get the new text, reset the template to its default in the editor.

Correction sends two things: A system prompt: the mode or template text, input-handling instructions, Dictionary corrections, and the active word list The text to correct Sogon doesn't send previous utterances or conversation history, and it doesn't send screen region images to the LLM either.
documents.s: What is sent to the LLM

documents.t: Sogon only asks for a permission when you press a button. Launching the app, changing settings, or starting a recording never opens a permission dialog. Settings → General → Permissions shows the current state as Granted, Denied, Not determined, or Unavailable. Permission Required Needed for Where to request it Microphone Yes All recording Settings → General → Permissions → Microphone Request Accessibility Yes Global shortcuts, pasting at the cursor, restoring editor focus Settings → General → Permissions → Accessibility Request System Audio (Screen Recording) No Recording system audio Settings → General → Permissions, or Request System Audio Permission in the quick controls Automation · Google Chrome No Restoring Chrome tabs and fields Settings → General → Permissions → Allow Automation · iTerm2 No Restoring iTerm2 sessions and tmux, Ask a CLI Settings → General → Permissions → Allow Automation · Notes No Send to Notes macOS asks the first time you send

macOS won't show the dialog again for a permission you denied once. In Settings → General → Permissions, press Open Settings next to the item to open the right page in System Settings, and turn Sogon on there. If shortcuts don't respond right after you allow Accessibility, quit and relaunch Sogon.
With default settings, audio and text don't leave your Mac. Sogon sends them to a service only when you turn on one of the conditions below.

Data Stored by default in Sent when Sent to Dictation transcriptions Local history You choose a cloud LLM provider That provider Microphone and system audio Memory, or local WAV You choose Groq Cloud as the STT engine Groq Meeting audio Local session folder You turn on AWS Transcribe and start a transcription S3 and Transcribe in your AWS account ⌘C twice source text Local translation history (7 days, 100 items) Translation is on and you press the second ⌘C Your LLM provider Selected text in the ⌃⇧C grid Not stored You press a correct, structure, translate, or template cell Your LLM provider Snippet name suggestions Local snippets Suggest a name is on; the first 500 characters Your LLM provider Screen region images Local history Never sent; pasted into the target app through the clipboard The app you paste into Dictionary App settings Active words are included as a glossary in LLM correction Your LLM provider The LLM provider defaults to None (use raw transcript). AWS Transcribe, translation, screen region, and text correction from external tools are all off by default.

Item Location How to delete Dictation history App settings and ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/ Delete in Settings → History, or set a retention period Recordings (when kept) ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/Recordings/ Delete the history item Meeting sessions Session folders under ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/ Delete the meeting item, or Delete audio Translation history App settings Deleted automatically after 7 days, or delete in History API keys macOS Keychain Clear the field in Settings → LLM or STT Debug logs ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/Logs/ Turn logging off and delete the folder

Debug logging is off by default. Even when on, it records states and character counts, never content such as transcriptions, translations, or copied text. Sogon masks keys, tokens, home folder paths, and URL queries. Details are in Send diagnostics.

Open Settings from the settings button in the quick controls (click the menu bar icon) or from the Dock icon. There are eight tabs at the top. Tab Main purpose Status The same controls as the quick controls: start and stop recording, cancel, audio sources, engines, last transcription, update notices General Shortcuts, recording mode, input sources, external tools, context restore, where the app appears, diagnostics, permissions STT Speech recognition engine and options, live preview, AWS Transcribe LLM Correction provider and key, model, correction mode, prompt templates Models Downloaded STT models, sizes, deletion, download progress Dictionary Word sets, terms, corrections, import and export Snippets Snippet list, name suggestions, send-out URL actions History Dictation, meeting, and translation history, file import, retention

In Settings → General → General → Show app in, choose Menu bar only, Menu bar + Dock, or Dock only. The default is Menu bar + Dock. If the MacBook notch or other menu bar apps hide the icon, you can still open Settings from the Dock. The change applies immediately, without a restart.
In Settings → General → General → Interface Language, pick System, Korean, or English. It defaults to System and is independent of the transcription language.
Change global shortcuts in Settings → General → Recording. Reset to Default next to each one restores the default below.

Default Setting name Action Default state ⌃⇧R Global Shortcut Dictation. With Push to Talk, records while held; with Toggle, press to start and again to stop. On ⌃⇧D Dictation Shortcut Press-to-start, press-to-stop dictation regardless of the recording mode. Also works during a meeting recording. On ⌃⇧⌫ Cancel Shortcut Discards the dictation in progress. Does nothing when only a meeting session is running. On ⌃⇧T Text Input Shortcut Opens the input window for correcting without speaking. On ⌃⇧C Selection Action Shortcut Opens the action grid for the selected text. On ⌃⇧V Snippet Shortcut Opens the snippet palette. On ⌃⇧S Screen Region Shortcut Captures a screen region and records. Press again to submit. Works after turning it on in External Tools ⌃⇧E Screen Translate Shortcut Captures a screen region, reads its text, and translates it. Works after turning it on in External Tools ⌘C twice Not configurable Translates the selected text. Works after turning it on in External Tools Registered global shortcuts reach Sogon before other apps. If one collides with another app's shortcut, that combination stops working in the other app, so pick a different one. ⌘C twice is the exception: it only observes copying and never blocks it.

Window Key Action Text input ⌘Return Submit esc Close Snippet palette ⏎ Insert at the cursor ⌘1–⌘9 Insert by number from the visible list ⌘⏎ Put on the clipboard Action grid 1–4, q–r, a–f Choose a cell esc Close. In the Aa sub-grid, go back to the main grid. Translation and rewrite result ⏎ Replace c Copy esc Discard Large type + / − / 0 Bigger / smaller / reset Screen region ⌘Return or ⌃⇧S Submit Quick controls ⌘Q Quit Sogon esc never cancels dictation. Capturing esc globally would stop other apps from receiving it.

Choose in Settings → STT → Speech Recognition Engine. Engine Where it runs Needs Notes WhisperKit (local) On your Mac A model download Picking a model in the tutorial selects this engine. Live preview and pause line breaks work only here. MLX Audio (local) On your Mac uv installed The default when you skip the tutorial and uv is available. The default model is Qwen3-ASR-1.7B-8bit. Groq Cloud (fast) Cloud Groq API key Audio is sent to Groq.

A model downloads as soon as you pick it. See progress and sizes in the Settings → Models tab. Model Size Character Tiny about 150MB Fastest, but hard to use for Korean. Base about 290MB Often gets proper nouns and technical terms wrong. Small about 970MB The lower bound where Korean becomes usable. Large v3 Turbo about 1.6GB Default. Balanced speed and accuracy Large v3 Turbo (v20240930) about 1.6GB A later snapshot of the same family Large v3 Turbo compressed about 632MB Smaller and faster than the default, with lower CPU use. Large v3 quantized about 947MB A smaller version of Large v3 Large v3 about 3.1GB Most accurate and slowest. If transcription is slow, check Activity Monitor for other apps using the CPU before switching models. When specific terms keep coming out wrong, adding them to the Dictionary is quicker than a bigger model. Models are stored in ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/Sogon/Models/whisperkit.
Find the symptom and work from the top down. If that doesn't solve it, create diagnostics and send them.

In Settings → General → Permissions, check that Accessibility shows Granted. If you just granted it, quit and relaunch Sogon. If it fails only in one app, check whether that app's Secure Keyboard Entry (iTerm2 and others) is on. When it is, it blocks global shortcuts. In Settings → General → Recording, check that the shortcut doesn't collide with another app's. ⌘C twice and ⌃⇧S work only after you turn them on in Settings → General → External Tools.

Situation What to do The result is only on the clipboard You may not have finished the tutorial with Get started. In Settings → General → Tutorial → Show again, press Get started on the last screen. The Voice Bar says it left the result on the clipboard There was no field to paste into, or pasting was blocked. Paste with ⌘V. Remote desktop, virtual machine, password field Synthesized paste cannot reach these. Paste the clipboard contents yourself. The result is empty You spoke too briefly or the input level was low. Check that the Voice Bar level moves and try again.
documents.s: Recording works but no text is inserted

documents.t: With several displays, clicking the menu bar on another display sends the text to that display's app. Use the shortcut instead. If you switched Chrome tabs or iTerm2 sessions while recording, turn on Settings → General → Context Restore and grant the Automation permission.
documents.s: Text goes to the wrong place

documents.t: Check that the provider in Settings → LLM is not None. Check that the correction provider's Status is not an error. If it is, enter the key again. Check that Enable correction is on in the quick controls. Sogon inserts text longer than 1,500 characters without correcting it. In Standard and Filler Removal modes, if the correction changes more than half the original, Sogon keeps the original.

Check that the translation switch in Settings → General → External Tools is on. Check that text is actually selected. With no selection, ⌘C copies nothing, so there's nothing to translate. If the two ⌘C presses are further apart than the macOS double-click speed, nothing is translated.
documents.s: The translation window does not appear

documents.t: By default sessions are Record only, do not transcribe. Expand the item in Settings → History → Meetings and press Start transcription. Even sessions that transcribe while recording show the first result after at least 2 minutes. Minutes sessions don't show the transcription while recording. Use Show session transcript in a verbatim session.
documents.s: The meeting transcription is not visible

documents.t: Speaker sound leaked back into the mic and both tracks transcribed it. It stays visible during recording, and Sogon removes most of it from outputs. Headphones avoid it. The limits are in Known issues.
documents.s: The same speech appears twice when using speakers

documents.t: Open Settings → History. With no meeting history, Sogon shows a separate Import files section; with meeting history, choose Meetings in the switcher and look at the top of the list. In earlier versions (v0.31.1 and below), the button didn't show when there was no meeting history at all.
documents.s: The Import files button is missing

documents.t: Sending a diagnostics file with your report makes the cause much faster to find. The file holds environment details and recent logs, and never content such as dictated text or translations.

In Settings → General → Diagnostics, turn on Write debug log. Do the action that caused the problem once more. Press Export diagnostics in the same section. A file named Sogon-진단-<date>-<time>.txt appears on your desktop. Send this file. When you are done, turn Write debug log off again. Sogon records nothing that happened before you turned logging on, so reproduce the problem after turning it on.

Contents Examples Environment App version, macOS version, Accessibility trust, whether the event tap is running, Secure Event Input state Settings summary Shortcuts, recording mode, STT provider, overlay display Recent logs Shortcut triggers, permission states, transcription and correction stages, insertion results, restore failure reasons and character counts

Transcriptions, corrected text, translations, copied text, snippet bodies API keys and tokens. Anything that slips in is replaced with <redacted>. The user name in home folder paths, replaced with ~ URL queries and fragments

Location: ~/Library/Application Support/Sogon/Logs/. Open it with Open log folder. The folder and files are readable only by your account. When sogon.log reaches 5MB it rolls over to sogon.1.log once and starts fresh. One event is one line, and a line never exceeds 2,000 characters.

Twice, a long meeting session stopped producing segments or its elapsed time froze. Other sessions under the same conditions were fine, and the cause is still unknown. If the elapsed time stays frozen for several minutes, press Stop Recording. The audio up to that point is kept. If debug logging was on, please send diagnostics.

Without headphones, the microphone picks up system audio again. Both tracks show as is during recording. Outputs remove the duplicates, with limits: Sogon removes leaked sound during stretches where you are not talking. Stretches where you talk during playback are kept so your own words aren't deleted. The leaked sentences in those stretches may remain twice. On some Macs the microphone input is louder than system audio, and the volume-based check doesn't trigger. Headphones avoid this issue.
documents.s: The same speech appears twice when using speakers

documents.t: Before v0.13.0, Sogon silently dropped parts of stretches longer than 30 seconds. If the audio is still there, expand the history item and use Transcribe again. It creates a new session and leaves the original untouched.
documents.s: Long recordings transcribed before v0.13.0 are missing content
